episodes.168249: A backdoor cold front that moved through eastern and central New Mexico on June 1, 2022, ushered in low-level moisture and helped to set the stage for thunderstorm development during the afternoon of June 2nd. As the atmophere destabilized, thunderstorms developed along the high terrain as well as along the dryline. The highest severe weather threat for the day was across south central New Mexico where the nose of an upper-level jet provided the best wind shear. Hail and severe winds were the primary threats of the day, and a thunderstorm near Gran Quivira was reported to have quarter size hail. In southern Socorro County, wind gusts in excess of 60 mph were reported along thunderstorm outflow.
episodes.168259: Strong to severe thunderstorms produced gusty winds over the tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay.

episodes.168268: A somewhat unusual convective environment developed on June 1. A wedge of warm, unstable air existed in between a backdoor cold front dropping from northeast to southwest and another cold front moving in from the west. This shrinking area of warm air was characterized by moderate to strong instability but only weak to moderate shear. A few areas of convection developed while conditions remained favorable, which produced localized instances of damaging winds and hail.

episodes.168270: A cold front moved through the mid-Atlantic on June 2. A diffuse backdoor cold front that have moved into the area the prior day was also present near the Delmarva peninsula and southern New Jersey. A rather complex convective environment developed ahead of the approaching front, generally characterized by both moderate shear and instability. Widespread thunderstorm activity developed ahead of the front, with a mixed mode of multicells and a couple of supercells. Some of the storms became severe as they moved through the region, producing damaging winds and small hail. As the front moved offshore during the later evening hours, the severe weather threat diminished and a cooler, drier air mass settled in.

episodes.168348: A cluster of thunderstorms focused near Cleveland became organized (into a squall line) the evening of June 1st and unleashed strong damaging wind north and west of Pittsburgh. The environment was prime for strong storms to occur: mean layer CAPE was near 1500 J/kg at the time of the squall line and effective bulk shear ranged between 30-35kts. Storms lost their intensity as they approached Pittsburgh and a gust front jetted out ahead of the line of convection, approaching an area that lacked robust instability.

episodes.168535: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to parts of northern New Jersey on the evening of June 1.  Rainfall totals as high as 2 to 3 inches fell in a short amount of time.
episodes.168645: Cooler air was ushered into the region early on the first with an outflow boundary reinforced front. This front settled across the southern South Plains in the afternoon leaving a stout elevated mixed layer across the remainder of the South Plains and southern Texas Panhandle. Isolated elevated supercells developed within this instability across the extreme southern Texas Panhandle. Some of these storms became severe producing hail up to baseball size near Matador causing vehicle damage (Motley County).
episodes.168766: A cold front crossing through the Central Appalachians during peak heating hours allowed for isolated showers and thunderstorms to sprout in southwestern Virginia. A few of these storms were strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts, which resulted in downed trees and power lines in Dickenson County during the late morning and early afternoon hours of June 2nd.
episodes.169037: A surface cold front drifted southeastward from southeastern Lower MI and northwest OH to western NY, northwest PA, and northeast OH during the afternoon through late evening of the 1st as an occluded low meandered over northeast MB. Ahead of the front, multicell thunderstorm clusters, many of which grew upscale into a longer squall line, impacted northern OH as the storms evolved generally eastward. In vicinity of the front, a supercell moved generally eastward across northwest OH before merging with nearby thunderstorms and evolving into a multicell storm cluster. These storms occurred within a warm sector comprised of moderate to strong effective bulk shear and primarily moderate MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively. There were multiple reports of severe hail and damaging convective wind gusts.
episodes.169213: Several loosely organized clusters of thunderstorms produced localized strong wind gusts and isolated hail. The lack of greater vertical wind shear limited organization of the storms. A cold front moved south-southeast from the Plains and Great Lakes, preceded by multiple thunderstorm outflow boundaries. The storms reached their peak intensity during the late afternoon and early evening, when the diurnal peak of instability was reached.
episodes.169215: Several loosely organized clusters of thunderstorms produced localized strong wind gusts and isolated hail. The lack of greater vertical wind shear limited organization of the storms. A cold front moved south-southeast from the Plains and Great Lakes, preceded by multiple thunderstorm outflow boundaries. The storms reached their peak intensity during the late afternoon and early evening, when the diurnal peak of instability was reached.
episodes.169328: A cold front was moving into Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. A dryline bisected the cold front and extended southward into the Big Bend. Plentiful low-level moisture was across the area ahead of the dryline. This moisture combined with temperatures in the mid-90s ahead of the cold front and resulted in an unstable atmosphere. Moderate wind shear was across the area. Lingering outflow boundaries from current and previous thunderstorms also aided in lift. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms that produced hail and strong winds across West Texas and Southeast New Mexico.
episodes.169632: A few rounds of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms moved across East Tennessee during the afternoon hours of June 2. Some of the storms produced damaging wind gusts, with one storm producing large hail.
episodes.169633: A few rounds of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms moved across southwest Virginia during the late morning and afternoon hours of June 2. A few of the storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170379: North and Central Texas began June with an unsettled weather pattern in place. An upper level disturbance and weak front worked together to generate multiple rounds of showers and storms. Outflow boundaries from earlier convection also served as a focus for development in succeeding time periods. A few severe storms occurred, along with localized areas of flash flooding, and two fatalities occurred due to flooding.
episodes.170536: A cold front passed through southwestern and central VA, interacting with an unstable air mass and limited shear to produce severe thunderstorms. Several of these storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.170544: A cold front passed through WV, interacting with an unstable air mass and limited shear to produce severe thunderstorms. A few of these storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.170548: A cold front passed through North Carolina, interacting with an unstable air mass and limited shear to produce severe thunderstorms . Several of these storms generated damaging winds.
episodes.170549: Thunderstorms developed across north central Oklahoma and south central Kansas on May 31st near an outflow boundary, and moved through southeastern Kansas, far northeastern Oklahoma, and southwestern Missouri during the early morning hours of June 1st. Widespread heavy rainfall of up to six inches in southeastern Kansas, resulted in moderate flooding of the Neosho River near Commerce.
episodes.170630: During the early morning hours on June 2nd, a convective complex moved across north central Kentucky in a warm and unstable environment just ahead of a surface cold front. On the leading edge of the system, strong to severe storms cause isolated wind damage across Jefferson and Scott County.
episodes.170747: A weak upper trough drifted south into East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon of June 2nd, with ongoing showers and thunderstorms that morning over Southwest Arkansas and Northeast Texas able to reinforce a weak cold front south into East Texas and North Louisiana. This boundary was able to focus renewed thunderstorm development during the afternoon over North-central Louisiana, with an isolated severe thunderstorm developing over Natchitoches. This storm produced damaging winds which downed a large tree and destroyed an outbuilding on the campus of Northwestern State University.
episodes.170779: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed across central, northern, and eastern Virginia as well as the Maryland Eastern Shore on June 2nd in response to a surface trough and upstream MCV.
episodes.170786: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed across central, northern, and eastern Virginia as well as the Maryland Eastern Shore on June 2nd in response to a surface trough and upstream MCV.

episodes.170829: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina mountains and foothills during early-to-mid afternoon and steadily developed into the Piedmont during mid-to-late afternoon. A few of the storms produced hail and brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170830: Scattered thunderstorms developed near the Blue Ridge escarpment during the afternoon and drifted south into the South Carolina foothills. A couple of the storms produced hail and brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171191: A weak frontal boundary drifted into the region during the afternoon of the 2nd sparking scattered thunderstorms. The boundary lingered in the region for a few days causing thunderstorms through the 5th.
episodes.171230: Storms developed along a stationary boundary in northwestern Oklahoma into the Texas panhandle during the afternoon and evening of May 31st, and lingered into the early morning hours of June 1st. Slow storm motions led to very heavy rainfall and a few reports of hail were also received.
episodes.171440: Isolated evening severe thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts across West Central Texas.
episodes.171487: An extended period of hazardous marine winds, resultant from showers and thunderstorms, impacted the Florida Keys coastal waters in association with a slowly-developing low pressure system originating near the Yucatan Peninsula.  The low pressure, monitored for tropical cyclone development and designated as Potential Tropical Cyclone One, moved northeast and crossed the southern Florida peninsula the morning of June 4th.  The low pressure later attained the organization necessary to become Tropical Storm Alex well east of Florida.  As the low pressure required potential tropical cyclone advisories, a detailed report of maximum winds in the Florida Keys marine area is available from the MIAPSHKEY product (WMO Header ACUS72 KKEY) issued on June 7, 2022.

episodes.171603: A cold front sparked off heavy thunderstorms that slowly moved though northeast New Jersey and the NYC metro area. These thunderstorms dropped between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain in less than 2 hours which resulted in areas of flash flooding.
